text.p: The New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) is to explore the concept of a "market-maker" program to help launch a possible new copper contract or any other new market, NYMEX President Patrick Thompson said.
"We are looking to develop a market-maker program for new contracts to hasten liquidity," Thompson told Reuters.
At present it is difficult to launch new contracts effectively. Initially, it is often not easy to attract resources and the brokerage interest without diluting existing markets, he said.
Thus, NYMEX is looking at getting selected highly-capitalised market-makers to take on a requirement to make markets and trade minumum volumes.

This will help to get a new contract, such as copper for delivery outside the U.S., up and running. Once liquidity develops, then it will be phased out. The concept is not without precedent - it has been utilised for stock options in the Chicago exchanges, he noted.
Initially, this programme will be developed for open-outcry trading in the pits, but it is hoped that it can be extended to NYMEX's after-hours ACCESS electronic trading system, Thompson said.
"We have to take steps to support the development of contracts," he said.
On Tuesday NYMEX told an industry gathering that its COMEX division copper advisory committee had decided to move ahead and open a warehouse in Chile to take delivery of its copper futures contract.
Opening the Chilean warehouse will present difficult and complex issues, Thompson said. "I would hope some time this year we would have some answers."

NYMEX spoke to Codelco, the world's biggest copper producer and to other Chilean miners about the proposed warehouse. "Their response has been positive but it is going too far to say they embraced the idea," Thompson said.
And some U.S. copper producers were still concerned that a foreign COMEX warehouse could cause uncertainty in the market.

"We believe we would probably not open warehouses for delivery against our current contract," Thompson said. "It may entail having a separate futures contract that would trade in parallel with the existing futures contract."
The market maker program would help nurture the second copper contract during its infancy.
NYMEX is also eyeing Singapore as a copper warehouse location and the Singapore Commodity Exchange (SICOM) was receptive to the idea, Thompson said.
Meanwhile Thompson insisted that the long standing project to relaunch a New York aluminum futures contract was still alive.
"We continue to look at the aluminum issue. The market maker program would be equally appliable to an aluminum contract," Thompson said.
((Martin Hayes and Huw Jones, New York Commodities 212-859-1646))
